summary: The outcome-led pilot and ROUTINEV3 source extension keep one accountable owner, one meaningful independent exact-source review, relevant tests, final required CI and exact tested-versus-delivered correspondence. Reviewer independence means separation from implementation authorship; an authorized fresh subagent may perform review where the platform permits, without a universal second-human collaborator requirement. Accepted author-run Home source tests are reused rather than repeated solely for reviewer independence; changed inputs, missing evidence or a concrete unresolved defect justify affected retesting. Final required CI remains mandatory. Review-role separation does not replace distinct credential custody or independent operational trust-boundary readback. A cybersecurity-flagged reviewer turn leaves the affected AUTH review incomplete; its observed failure does not establish a separate Auto-review denial, a universal prohibition or an obligation for the sole maintainer to find human staffing. The correction neither retries nor reroutes AUTH review, and user authorization does not override platform restrictions. Existing issue/PR state, actual reviewer activation, canonical metadata preservation, protected governing activation, targeted reads for missing joins and no duplicate packet/status machinery remain. The v3 priorities stay with their existing owners, including SC2 Checks-read access and the named UTEL producer/provider journey. The separately accepted ADR-0095 fresh-profile resource-containment contract remains distinct from the legacy ADR-0093 universal-copy proof profile: this review clarification changes neither contract nor admission. Unknown reservations, original .103 attempted-unknown/unreplayed and .104 held, restricted evidence, publication/installation/runtime boundaries and unsupported savings remain intact.
title: Outcome-led source delivery separates review authorship without mandatory human staffing
